subject: history
title: Japanese Expansion 1931-1941
welcome_lead: From the Mukden Incident to Pearl Harbor, study Japan's path to global war.
meta_desc: IBDP History Move to Global War Adventure 1: Japanese expansion in East Asia 1931-1941.
final_note: You have followed Japan's road from Manchuria to Hawaii. The international order set in 1919 collapsed in the Pacific.

concepts.def: Staged sabotage of the South Manchurian Railway used to justify Japanese seizure of Manchuria.
Puppet state established by Japan in Manchuria in 1932 under Pu Yi.
League of Nations enquiry condemning Japan's actions, prompting its withdrawal from the League.
Clash near Beijing that triggered full-scale war between Japan and China.
Mass killings and atrocities committed by Japanese forces after the fall of Nanjing.
Alliance between Germany, Italy and Japan formalising the Axis.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Kwantung Army's staged Mukden Incident on 18 September 1931 provided a pretext for seizing Manchuria. Civilian government in Tokyo failed to restrain the military. By 1932 the puppet state Manchukuo was proclaimed under the former Qing emperor Pu Yi. The League of Nations Lytton Commission (1932) condemned Japan, prompting Japanese withdrawal in 1933.

The Marco Polo Bridge Incident on 7 July 1937 ignited a full-scale Sino-Japanese War. Shanghai fell after fierce fighting; Nanjing was captured in December and subjected to atrocities still debated in scale. By 1938 Japan controlled much of coastal China but failed to defeat Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists or Mao's communists, who retreated inland.

Defeat by the USSR at Khalkhin Gol (1939), the Tripartite Pact (1940) and occupation of French Indochina (1940-41) prompted US embargoes including oil (July 1941). Diplomatic talks failed; Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941 alongside coordinated assaults on British, Dutch and American territories across Southeast Asia.
